$comment: The MCP live-UI push contract (phase C) shared by the Java, .NET and Python backends and the sidecar. See README.md, section 'Live UI push'. pushTools are normative byte for byte (listed after the eight base tools and before mateu_save_spec, only when push is enabled); scenario is run by each backend's test with the volatile values normalised: a session handle -> "<session:NAME>" (NAME = the UI session's sessionId), connectedAt -> "<time>", a pairing code -> "<code>", the requestId of a query message -> "<request>". The runners set the answer timeout (answer-timeout-ms) to a short value (300 ms): one query of the scenario is left unanswered.

pushTools.name: mateu_list_sessions
pushTools.description: List the live UI sessions (browser tabs, app windows) this caller may send UI to: its own (same signed-in user) and the ones paired to it with mateu_pair_session. Returns {sessions: [{session, user, route, renderer, connectedAt, connected, paired}]}.

pushTools.name: mateu_pair_session
pushTools.description: Pair a live UI session with this caller, using the one-time code the user sees after clicking "Connect AI" in the app. Returns the session; it can then be addressed by mateu_push_ui, mateu_navigate and mateu_dispatch_event. The code expires in minutes and works once.

code.description: the pairing code shown in the app, e.g. K7QF-4MZP

pushTools.name: mateu_push_ui
pushTools.description: Show a screen in a live UI session: validate the YAML page first (nothing is sent when it has errors), then render it in that tab, in the content area (default), a drawer or a dialog. Layout only: no view model is bound. Returns {delivered, session, target, validation} or {delivered: false, reason, validation}.

session.description: a session from mateu_list_sessions or mateu_pair_session

title.description: optional: the drawer's or dialog's header

pushTools.name: mateu_navigate
pushTools.description: Navigate a live UI session to a route of the app, like a click on the menu entry carrying these fields. Returns {delivered, session}.

session.description: a session from mateu_list_sessions or mateu_pair_session

consumedRoute.description: optional: the route consumed by the app shell (usually "")

actionId.description: optional: an action to run on arrival

baseUrl.description: optional: the base URL of the target micro-frontend

serverSideType.description: optional: the server-side type of the target UI

pushTools.name: mateu_dispatch_event
pushTools.description: Dispatch a named UI event in a live UI session, for the components that subscribe to it (@SubscribeTo). The built-in events are reserved: use mateu_push_ui and mateu_navigate for them. Returns {delivered, session}.

session.description: a session from mateu_list_sessions or mateu_pair_session

pushTools.name: mateu_get_session_screen
pushTools.description: Read what the user sees in a live UI session, as that tab draws it: route, window title, page header, fields (id, label, type, value, required, readOnly, error, options), the actions the user can press (id, label, enabled), the rows of each listing's current page with its search, filters, sort, page and total, an open dialog or drawer (focus: overlay, in front of the page) and the last messages. Only what the screen shows; long values and lists are capped and named in truncated. Returns {session, screen}.

session.description: a session from mateu_list_sessions or mateu_pair_session

pushTools.name: mateu_set_session_fields
pushTools.description: Type values into fields of the screen in a live UI session (the dialog's or drawer's when one is open), exactly as the user editing them: validation, client rules and the unsaved-changes state follow. Only fields the screen shows as editable: any other refuses the whole call and nothing changes. Returns {session, screen} after the change.

session.description: a session from mateu_list_sessions or mateu_pair_session

values.description: field id -> value (a string, number, boolean, or a list for a multi-value field)

pushTools.name: mateu_run_session_action
pushTools.description: Press an action the screen in a live UI session offers (an id from mateu_get_session_screen; a row action needs row), as the user clicking it: validation runs, and a confirmation the action asks for is shown to the user, who answers it. Returns {session, screen} once the screen settled.

session.description: a session from mateu_list_sessions or mateu_pair_session

parameters.description: optional: extra parameters of the action

row.description: optional, for a row action: the 0-based index of the row in the listing's rows

listing.description: optional, for a row action on a screen with several listings: the listing id

errors.rateLimited: Too many messages to this session; try again in a minute.

errors.frameworkEvent: Event "{event}" is one of the framework's own events: dispatch an event a screen subscribes to (@SubscribeTo).
errors.detailTooLarge: The detail is larger than the 65536-byte limit.
errors.invalidTarget: Invalid target "{target}": use content, drawer or dialog.
errors.channelRefused: This UI session belongs to another channel.
errors.tooManySessions: Too many live UI sessions; try again later.
errors.noAnswer: Session "{session}" did not answer in time.
errors.unknownField: Field "{id}" is not on the screen or cannot be edited.
errors.unknownAction: Action "{id}" is not offered by the screen.
errors.unknownRow: Row {id} is not on the current page of the listing.
errors.unsupported: This client does not support reading or operating its screen.
errors.failed: The UI could not complete the request.
errors.screenTooLarge: The screen the UI answered is larger than the 262144-byte limit.
errors.invalidRow: Invalid row: use the 0-based index of a row in the listing's rows.

reasons.hasErrors: The definition has errors; nothing was sent.
reasons.notAPage: Only a page (a component, or a layout: envelope) can be pushed.

scenario.$comment: UI sessions are opened in this order (sessionId, secret, principal or null, route, renderer). Callers: alice / bob (signed-in principals), anon (no identity, no agent key). Each step: as (caller), and either tool+args (args strings may name a session as <session:ID>, a code as <code:ID> = the last code the UI session ID asked for) with expect (the tool result JSON, or {error: text}), or ui (a UI-side operation: pair | unpair | disconnect) on sessionId, or received (the messages the session's channel received since the last check, in order, AgentPush data). The ui operation answer queues what the session answers ({screen} or {error: {code, id?}}, the parameters of _agent-screen besides sessionId/secret/requestId) to its NEXT query message, answered as soon as the message reaches it; a query with no answer queued is left unanswered.
